summary: Steel fire tower on Pike Knob in Pendleton County, now removed. Footings, concrete stairs and a ruined cabin remain in a Nature Conservancy preserve open by day.

facts.status_note: Tower removed; footings and concrete stairs remain.

access.note: Preserve open to the public during daylight hours, year-round. The old road is too rough for a passenger car after about two miles.

visit.trail_note: Unmarked, rocky trail, about 3 miles out and back; the former tower site is roughly 2 miles in.

notes_for_editor: No source gives a build year, so no built event was added; the 1930s and 90-foot height come from one 2026 hiking guide (cite 2) only. Agency conflict: the register names The Nature Conservancy; the Mon guide says the Forest Service and the Conservancy jointly manage the area; the eastern lookouts page header (easternuslookouts.weebly.com/pike-knob.html) reads 'National Forest'. The record's ownership 'federal' is not clearly wrong, since TNC's page says the old road reaches national forest land, but the site itself is in a TNC preserve; left for an editor. No staffing, fire or closure-date sources were found. The register photo (Brian Powell) is already in the record and was not re-added.
